security_audit.summary: Contextual review dismissed 36 static alerts caused by Markdown fences, inline code, metadata URLs, and fixed repository links. The user-derived output filename lacks an explicit sanitization rule, so a crafted name could escape the intended memory directory.

remediation.issue: The save path uses a user-derived preference or segment name without an explicit filename safety rule.
remediation.suggestion: Slugify the name to lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens, reject separators and dot segments, then verify the resolved path stays under the memory directory.

content.user_title: Design Email Preference and Frequency Controls
content.value_statement: Rising unsubscribe rates often show that subscribers lack practical topic and cadence choices. This skill designs preference controls and maps every choice to enforceable email rules.
actual_capabilities: Defines topic groups subscribers can independently enable or mute.
Creates at least two cadence tiers plus a time-limited pause option.
Orders frequency, topic, pause, and unsubscribe choices into an opt-down ladder.
Maps each preference to a specific suppression or sending-frequency rule.
Produces a SEND N sub-item assessment with Pass, Partial, or Fail rationale.
limitations: Does not implement settings in an ESP or call keyed provider APIs.
Does not maintain canonical consent, opt-out, or suppression records.
Does not design lifecycle flows, global send caps, or quiet hours.
Does not calculate the full SEND score or decide the N1 unsubscribe veto.

use_cases.title: Reduce subscriber fatigue
use_cases.description: Create weekly, monthly, and pause choices for a high-frequency promotional segment.

use_cases.title: Translate preferences into platform rules
use_cases.description: Map topic toggles and cadence choices to ESP suppression and throttling behavior.

use_cases.title: Review opt-out integrity
use_cases.description: Check that every step-down option remains optional and full unsubscribe stays immediately available.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic preference center
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a preference center for [product] subscribers. Use topics [list] and weekly, monthly, and 90-day pause options.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start with known topics and simple cadence choices.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an unsubscribe path
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this current unsubscribe path: [description]. Identify gaps, then design an opt-down ladder with a clearly available full unsubscribe.
prompt_templates.scenario: Replace a hard-opt-out-only path with optional step-down choices.

prompt_templates.title: Map preferences to ESP rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Using this ESP preference export and segment context, define fields, choice-to-rule mappings, source labels, and unresolved implementation questions: [paste data].
prompt_templates.scenario: Turn existing configuration data into an implementation specification.

prompt_templates.title: Align an advanced preference architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a preference architecture for [profile] across [topics]. Align tiers with [flow plan], define sunset conditions, and emit the SEND N sub-item note.
prompt_templates.scenario: Coordinate complex preference controls with lifecycle cadence and audit requirements.

output_examples.input: Build a preference center for a software newsletter with product, education, and event topics.
output: Fields: Product updates, education, events, cadence, and pause duration.
Ladder: Monthly, topic-only, 90-day pause, then full unsubscribe.
Rules: Each selection maps to a stream suppression or frequency cap.

output_examples.input: Assess a page that offers weekly and monthly email but no pause option.
output_examples.output: SEND N sub-item: Partial. Topic and cadence controls exist, but the page needs a pause option and an explicit rule for each choice.

best_practices: Keep full unsubscribe visible and immediately available at every opt-down stage.
Offer only cadence tiers that email operations can enforce reliably.
Label evidence as measured, user-provided, or estimated and confirm uncertain topic groups.
anti_patterns: Do not hide or delay unsubscribe behind preference choices.
Do not let a topic mute suppress unrelated email streams.
Do not invent cadence promises that existing lifecycle flows cannot honor.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the audience, topic groups, current cadence, ESP, and existing unsubscribe path. An export is helpful but not required.

faq.question: Does this skill configure my ESP?
faq.answer: No. It produces field and rule specifications for an operator or integration to implement.

faq.question: Does this replace legal review?
faq.answer: No. It supports subscriber choice, but legal review remains necessary for applicable consent and unsubscribe requirements.

faq.question: Where are preference decisions stored?
faq.answer: A consent registry or ESP must store and enforce the resulting preference, opt-out, and suppression records.

faq.question: Can it work without an ESP export?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use stated topics and default weekly, monthly, and pause tiers while marking assumptions as estimated.

faq.question: What does the final deliverable include?
faq.answer: It includes a field specification, ordered opt-down ladder, rule mapping, SEND N sub-item note, and handoff summary.
